qs.q: A patient is diagnosed with Stevens-Johnson syndrome following a severe drug reaction. Which morphological feature differentiates Toxic Epidermal Necrolysis from milder forms of this hypersensitivity spectrum?
o: Necrosis extends through the full thickness of the epidermis, causing large areas to slough off
Spongiosis with stretched intercellular bridges and superficial perivascular lymphocytic infiltrate
Lesions are strictly limited to pressure-bearing areas like the feet and buttocks
The presence of honey-colored crusts composed of dried serum and bacterial cocci
qs.e: Toxic Epidermal Necrolysis features full-thickness epidermal necrosis leading to extensive epidermal sloughing and fluid loss, unlike milder localized forms. Spongiosis is the hallmark of acute eczematous dermatitis rather than TEN.
